objective: Synchronizing partitions with a data catalog
secondaryObjectives: Building and referencing a technical data catalog: AWS Glue Data Catalog and the Apache Hive metastore

sources.cite: AWS Certification, AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate (DEA-C01) exam guide: Data Ingestion and Transformation 34%, Data Store Management 26%, Data Operations and Support 22%, Data Security and Governance 18%

sources.cite: Amazon Athena User Guide, MSCK REPAIR TABLE
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: MSCK REPAIR TABLE scans the table's location for Hive-compatible partitions (key=value folder names) added after the table was created and adds the missing ones to the Glue Data Catalog; 'for partitions that are not Hive-compatible, use ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION'; frequent use can cause timeouts, so ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION is recommended for daily additions. The Glue API reference (read 2026-11-18) lists BatchCreatePartition ('Creates one or more partitions in a batch operation'), the call the function makes; the Athena ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION page (read 2026-11-18) says LOCATION 'is required' for non-Hive-style data and names glue:CreatePartition for the DDL path. Partition projection, mentioned as an alternative, is from the Athena partitioning pages, not read this round.

brief.situation: You are the data engineer at Tallis Home, a fictional retailer. Click data lands hourly in s3://tallis-lake/clicks/YYYY/MM/DD/, and the Athena table clicks is partitioned by year, month and day. A small Lambda, add-partition, registers each new day's partition. Marketing's 10:00 report shows zero clicks for today.
handover: Yesterday a security cleanup removed 'unused' permissions from several Lambda roles.
The hourly load writes files once; running it again writes a second copy of the same hour.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the click files in S3, the Glue Data Catalog's partitions and the queries that read them.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the query found nothing, what you ran and why that statement, and what prevents tomorrow's repeat.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Separates the data from the catalog.
parts.modelAnswer: Today's files are in S3, but the catalog's last partition was 11/16. The add-partition function failed at 00:05 with AccessDenied on glue:BatchCreatePartition after yesterday's permission cleanup, so Athena never looked in today's folder.

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Picks the statement that fits the folder layout.
parts.modelAnswer: The folders are plain YYYY/MM/DD, not key=value, so MSCK REPAIR finds nothing. ALTER TABLE ADD IF NOT EXISTS PARTITION with the folder's location registered today. Re-running the loads would have doubled the data.

parts.label: Prevention
parts.modelAnswer: The role has glue:BatchCreatePartition again, on this table only, and a dry run shows tomorrow will register; the cleanup's owner knows why it is needed.

expertPath.text: SHOW PARTITIONS stops at 11/16; files present in plain date folders; add-partition AccessDenied; count 0.
ALTER TABLE ADD IF NOT EXISTS PARTITION with the location; restore the role's permission.

duplicated.headline: The data was fine; the catalog was not
duplicated.body: The files were already there. Re-running a load that writes once doubles the data. Register the partition; leave the data alone.

reportEmpty.headline: Athena reads only what the catalog lists
reportEmpty.body: A partitioned table reads only registered partitions. For folders that are not Hive-style, MSCK REPAIR finds nothing: add the partition with ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION.

synced.headline: Good: the catalog caught up, the cause removed
synced.body: You saw the files were there and the partition was not, used the statement that works for this folder layout, checked the count, and restored the one permission the daily function needs.

scoring.modelReasoning: The files are in S3 and the catalog's partitions stop yesterday, so Athena never reads today's folder; the function that adds partitions failed on a removed Glue permission. The folders are not Hive-style, so MSCK REPAIR cannot find them; ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION with the location registers today safely. Re-running the loads would double the data. Then restore that one permission and check tomorrow will work.
